findings.problem: The voice says what we must show (why c is at least four), but the board does not write the target until the very end, so the student has no written aim to work towards.
findings.fix: On "explain why C is at least four", write a line under the question such as `We want: why c ≥ 4`; the plan stays in the corner.

findings.problem: "Divide by X plus one" does not describe the move: the top is being rewritten in lots of (x + 1). The voice never says why we do this (to reach the form a + b/(x + 1)), and line 2 appears before any reason is given.
findings.fix: Say "To get the form A plus B over X plus one, write the top in terms of X plus one: four lots of X plus one make four X plus four, two too many, so take away two", and write line 2 on "write the top".

findings.problem: "Split the fraction" is said, but no split line is written. The board jumps from the single fraction to 4 − 2/(x + 1), and "is just four" gives no reason.
findings.fix: Write the next line of the whole equation, `y = \dfrac{4(x+1)}{x+1} - \dfrac{2}{x+1}`, on "Split the fraction". Light the first fraction and say "the top and bottom are the same, so it equals four" instead of "is just four".

findings.problem: One example (c = 2) shows a line below four cutting the curve. A student is not told why EVERY line below four must cut it, which is the half of the argument that rules out c < 4.
findings.fix: Add one sentence: "Near X equals negative one the curve goes down forever, and it climbs towards four, so it reaches every height below four. Any line below four cuts it."

findings.problem: The line y = c slides onto the dashed asymptote y = 4. Its label "c = 4" and the asymptote label "y = 4" sit at the same height, so they may overlap on a phone.
findings.fix: Check the phone frame and offset the "c = 4" label (for example to the other end of the line) so both labels can be read.
